reason: Rows 0-2 are sound: they match W2 v4 (2)(i) and S3/S7, W2a was used by probe 50 so W2b is the last 28 Sep slot, and the timing works (50 lands ~12:26-12:50Z, a non-CI file at 14:00Z ends ~21:50Z, a CI file at 12:00Z ends ~21:40-22:55Z, all before the 23:30Z freeze). Row 3 and Row 4 have defects, so the table should not be logged as written. (1) The premise that '50 is effectively the READMIT read' uses node counts (ILP 0.4 alone: +49 nodes). Fork counts on the 4-clip dummy say otherwise: exp85b (ILP 0.4 alone) has 84 forks vs 81 for exp70g (+3), exp85c (READMIT 0.94 alone) has 82 (+1), exp85a has 85 (+4). So ILP 0.4 carries 3 of the 4 extra forks, half the size of the cap 4->6 step (75->81 forks), which moved the board +0.002. The 743929 author also says both gains were node-neutral and came from re-wiring edges, so node count is the wrong test for 'inert'. A '-' on 50 cannot be pinned on READMIT: it may come from ILP 0.4's forks or from our base's READMIT->lowrefine coupling (+3.05% refined). (2) The R- branch, READMIT 0.98, is therefore a confounded 'other direction' read. 0.98 is not a disclosed value (743929 gives only 0.965->0.94 and 1.2->0.4), and aggressive mode covers disclosed values. exp87f/g do not exist yet (experiments/ ends at exp86c) and would need a build, a new gate and a dummy by ~13:45Z. (3) Row 4 lets a Row-3 file without a PASSED dummy leave the last slot unused, even though exp81, exp85b and exp85c already have PASSED dummies. exp86c's dummy was still only queued ('when a lane frees') at 06:37Z. (4) Minor: in Row 2 (exp83b, CI) and in Row 3 R0 (exp81, SEC), the last slot produces a public-only file (finals card: CI info-only; SEC excluded while Q3 is open). D12 also fires on a tie where v3 (5) would make exp78a the BASE.
fix: Log 'W2b TABLE v5 (R24)' with Rows 0-2 unchanged and this Row 3/4: Row 3 (wait for 50, latest 14:00Z): R+ -> D0 exp86c / D8 exp86a (unchanged). State the D12 tie case explicitly: disp78b == disp78a, both '+' -> D12 (S3 text), noting that BASE is exp78a under v3 (5).
